plain_english: The high-yield CCN-51 Ecuadorian bean becomes deliverable at the $80 premium; Ecuador later becomes the largest certified origin.

new: 250 t/day (up to 30,000 t held) or 500 t/day; load-out within 60 days
plain_english: Warehouses must ship certified cocoa at a minimum daily pace.
source_note: Resolution No. 2 XI adopted Dec 5 2014, eff. May 1 2015

old: Main Crop designations; Tanzania, Uganda, Para (Brazil) in Group C
new: Main/Mid/Light crop labels removed; Tanzania, Uganda, Para to Group B (+$80); Lome renamed Togo
plain_english: Removes crop-timing labels; three origins gain $80/t.
source_note: ICE Submission 20-10 (Jan 14 2020), eff. Jan 30 2020 for all months from March 2020

old: group named on the sample order; over-count lots rejected
new: class (premium group) set by the bean count found at grading; over 1,400 beans/kg not deliverable
plain_english: Fewer rejections: a West African lot with too high a count is certified at the Group B or C premium instead of failing.
source_note: ICE Submission 20-10, eff. Apr 1 2020, from the May 2020 contract

new: $400/t premium on Ivory Coast and Ghana forward sales
plain_english: Not an exchange rule: West African beans cost $400/t more physically, but ICE pays only +$160 for Group A, so they are rarely delivered.

old: bags of the weight customary for the growth
new: bags 45-75 kg for all growths; 'Chop' defined
plain_english: Clear bag-weight standard; no change in value (ICE).
source_note: ICE Submission 24-137 (Sep 13 2024); rulebook notes: amended Jun 20 2024, eff. Oct 1 2024

new: cocoa for grading must be customs cleared and free of duties, taxes and tariffs
plain_english: Any US tariff on an origin is paid before the cocoa can be certified.
source_note: Resolution No. 1 adopted Apr 8 2025, eff. Apr 8 2025

new: 10 t ±1%; 9.5-9.9 t partial default (higher of $11/t or 5% of price on the shortfall); over 10.3 t invoiced at 10.3 t; pro forma at 90% without weight note
source_note: Rulebook amendment note: amended Jun 20 2024, eff. Apr 24 2026
